outcomes: Describe symptom location, pattern, distribution, and progression before assigning a cause.
Collect environmental, root-zone, and plant observations in one traceable record.
Rank multiple plausible causes and identify evidence that supports or weakens each one.
Document follow-up observations so a diagnosis can be revised when new evidence appears.

exercises.title: Blind symptom description
exercises.task: Choose one plant image or real observation and write a description that contains no diagnosis words. Record tissue age, canopy position, pattern, distribution, severity, and progression.
exercises.deliverable: A completed plant-health intake record plus a short list of observations that are still missing.

exercises.title: Measurement-context audit
exercises.task: Take one suspected plant-health problem and identify which measurements would materially change the differential. Separate measurements you have from measurements you are assuming.
exercises.deliverable: A measurement checklist with instrument, location, timing, and uncertainty notes.

capstone.title: Evidence packet and ranked differential
capstone.brief: Build a complete evidence packet for one plant-health scenario without jumping directly from appearance to treatment.

outcomes: Identify major seed structures and connect them to germination.
Distinguish imbibition, radicle emergence, cotyledon opening, and first true-leaf development.
Separate seed viability questions from environmental establishment failures.
Record germination as a repeatable batch process rather than a memory-based result.

exercises.title: Seed anatomy reconstruction
exercises.task: Create a labeled seed cutaway from memory, then compare it with the Atlas reference and correct every misplaced or missing structure.
exercises.deliverable: A corrected labeled diagram with one sentence describing the role of each major structure.

exercises.title: Germination batch record
exercises.task: Track one germination batch by lot identity, setup, temperature, moisture approach, radicle emergence, cotyledon opening, abnormal seedlings, and non-germinated seeds.
exercises.deliverable: A completed seed and germination record with a calculated germination percentage and notes on uncertainty.

capstone.title: Seed-to-seedling establishment protocol
capstone.brief: Design an establishment workflow that preserves seed-lot identity and makes failures diagnosable.
evidence: Changes proposed for the next batch

outcomes: Distinguish primary, lateral, fine-root, and root-hair functions.
Connect media water, oxygen, ions, microbes, and root temperature to root performance.
Interpret root appearance with texture, branching, and root-zone measurements rather than color alone.
Relate root-zone conditions to whole-plant water and nutrient behavior.

exercises.title: Root-system observation map
exercises.task: Inspect a root system or reference image and map fine-root density, branching, active tips, discoloration, texture, and the media zones occupied by roots.
exercises.deliverable: A root-zone sketch plus a list of observations that are direct evidence versus interpretation.

exercises.title: Irrigation-response comparison
exercises.task: Record pre-irrigation moisture, input volume, drainage, pH, EC, and plant posture across repeated irrigation events.
exercises.deliverable: An irrigation/root-zone log showing at least two events and a short interpretation of what changed.

capstone.title: Root-zone evidence model
capstone.brief: Explain a root-zone problem as an interacting water, oxygen, chemistry, temperature, and biological system.
evidence: A ranked list of plausible root-stress mechanisms

outcomes: Identify simplified stem tissues and their structural roles.
Separate xylem water transport from phloem source-to-sink transport.
Relate internode development to genotype, stage, light, temperature, and growth rate.
Describe mechanical injury in terms of support and transport rather than appearance alone.

exercises.title: Transport-path tracing
exercises.task: Trace one molecule of water from the root zone to a transpiring leaf and one unit of photosynthate from a source leaf toward a growing sink.
exercises.deliverable: A two-path transport diagram labeling xylem, phloem, source, sink, and the environmental forces that affect movement.

exercises.title: Stem injury assessment
exercises.task: Compare bending, crushing, pruning, and breakage and record what evidence would indicate intact support, restricted transport, or recovery.
exercises.deliverable: A damage-and-recovery observation table.

capstone.title: Whole-plant transport explanation
capstone.brief: Explain how roots, stems, leaves, and active sinks remain connected through transport and how one disrupted segment can affect the rest of the plant.

outcomes: Locate nodes, internodes, axillary buds, and active shoot tips.
Explain apical dominance and why branch responses differ after training.
Compare topping, directional training, mainlining, and screen-based canopy organization.
Evaluate training by canopy structure, light distribution, recovery, and plant condition instead of unsupported yield claims.

exercises.title: Branch-response map
exercises.task: Choose a training event and map the active shoot tips before and after it. Record which branches changed position or growth priority.
exercises.deliverable: A before/after branch map with node numbers and observation dates.

exercises.title: Canopy distribution audit
exercises.task: Record canopy height variation and visible high/low-light zones before and after a training adjustment.
exercises.deliverable: A canopy sketch with height bands, likely light zones, and the structural change made.

capstone.title: Training-system comparison
capstone.brief: Compare two training approaches using the same evaluation criteria rather than declaring one universally superior.

outcomes: Use a healthy leaf as a structural and visual baseline.
Connect photosynthesis to light, carbon dioxide, water status, and chloroplast function.
Relate stomata and transpiration to temperature, humidity, airflow, and root-water supply.
Describe leaf symptoms precisely before attempting diagnosis.

exercises.title: Healthy-leaf baseline plate
exercises.task: Document a healthy leaf using leaflet shape, venation, petiole, surface condition, color distribution, and posture.
exercises.deliverable: A labeled baseline image or drawing that can be reused for later comparisons.

exercises.title: Gas-exchange context record
exercises.task: Record temperature, RH, leaf-temperature context if available, airflow state, light context, and leaf posture at multiple times in one day.
exercises.deliverable: A time-series observation sheet explaining how atmospheric demand changed through the day.

capstone.title: Leaf function and symptom analysis
capstone.brief: Explain one leaf symptom without treating color or shape as a diagnosis by itself.
evidence: At least three plausible cause categories

outcomes: Identify major female flower structures across development.
Separate floral transition, stretch, bud development, pollination response, and senescence.
Use multiple maturity signals and representative sampling instead of a single visual cue.
Recognize disease and physical-risk observations that can complicate maturity decisions.

exercises.title: Flower-stage image series
exercises.task: Document the same flower site or a standardized set of sites across several dates and describe changes in bracts, stigmas, resin coverage, structure, and senescence.
exercises.deliverable: A dated development sequence with consistent sampling notes.

exercises.title: Representative maturity sampling
exercises.task: Define canopy positions and flower sites before inspecting maturity so sampling is not biased toward one convenient location.
exercises.deliverable: A completed harvest maturity sampling record from multiple representative sites.

capstone.title: Defensible harvest-readiness assessment
capstone.brief: Build a harvest-readiness decision from repeated representative observations rather than one photograph or one trichome field.

outcomes: Distinguish major glandular trichome forms and basic gland anatomy.
Standardize magnification, tissue sampled, lighting, and sampling location.
Treat clear/cloudy/amber appearance as one observation rather than a direct potency measurement.
Separate visible resin abundance from analytical cannabinoid or terpene chemistry.

exercises.title: Microscope sampling standard
exercises.task: Write a repeatable microscope workflow specifying tissue type, canopy position, magnification, illumination, and image labeling.
exercises.deliverable: A one-page sampling SOP and a labeled example image set.

exercises.title: Bract versus sugar-leaf comparison
exercises.task: Compare gland observations from flower bracts and nearby sugar leaves without assuming both tissues represent maturity equally.
exercises.deliverable: A side-by-side comparison with tissue identity and sampling limitations stated explicitly.

capstone.title: Trichome observation protocol
capstone.brief: Create a repeatable observation protocol that can support maturity tracking without claiming visual microscopy substitutes for laboratory chemistry.

outcomes: Distinguish developing staminate and pistillate reproductive structures.
Recognize mixed-sex expression as an observation that still requires context.
Explain pollen release, transport, stigma contact, fertilization, and seed development.
Use isolation, labels, records, and controlled handling to preserve cross identity.

exercises.title: Reproductive-structure identification
exercises.task: Classify a set of preflower and flower references by structure and developmental stage, including ambiguous examples that require more observation.
exercises.deliverable: An identification sheet with confidence notes and the evidence used for each classification.

exercises.title: Controlled-pollination record design
exercises.task: Design a record that preserves pollen source, target plant, target branch, date, isolation method, labels, and later seed observations.
exercises.deliverable: A controlled-pollination worksheet plus a contamination-prevention checklist.

capstone.title: Traceable cross plan
capstone.brief: Build a complete controlled-cross documentation plan from pollen source through mature seed lot.
evidence: Seed-lot identity and phenotype observation plan

outcomes: Treat temperature, humidity, VPD, airflow, light, leaf temperature, and root-zone water as interacting variables.
Distinguish instantaneous PPFD from daily light integral.
Map environmental variation across space rather than relying on one sensor or one light reading.
Use plant response and measurement context together when adjusting the environment.

exercises.title: Daily VPD context profile
exercises.task: Record temperature, RH, leaf-temperature context, light state, irrigation timing, airflow, and plant posture at several points through one light cycle.
exercises.deliverable: A completed VPD environment log with notes explaining when atmospheric demand changed most.

exercises.title: Canopy PPFD map
exercises.task: Measure a defined canopy grid rather than one center point and identify high-light, low-light, and uniform zones.
exercises.deliverable: A completed PPFD map with minimum, maximum, average, and a proposed adjustment if needed.

capstone.title: Environment interaction map
capstone.brief: Build a whole-system environmental assessment that connects atmospheric demand, photon delivery, airflow, and root-zone supply.

outcomes: Scout plants and production zones before damage becomes severe.
Identify pests by organism and life stage rather than damage alone.
Separate disease signs, symptoms, environmental stress, and systemic-pathogen questions.
Use quarantine, sanitation, clean stock, records, and compatible controls as one integrated system.

exercises.title: Scouting and hotspot map
exercises.task: Divide a crop or practice layout into repeatable zones and record pest life stages, damage, beneficial organisms, and monitoring-card observations separately.
exercises.deliverable: A completed scouting map with at least one scheduled recheck point.

exercises.title: Look-alike differential
exercises.task: Choose one symptom such as stippling, pale residue, distorted new growth, or root discoloration and compare at least three plausible explanations.
exercises.deliverable: A differential table showing evidence for, evidence against, and the next discriminating check for each possibility.

capstone.title: IPM and biosecurity response plan
capstone.brief: Build an evidence-based response plan for a confirmed or suspected plant-health problem while protecting unaffected stock.

outcomes: Evaluate outdoor sites by sun, drainage, wind, water, microclimate, biology, and seasonal risk.
Explain how protected structures change heat, humidity, condensation, ventilation, pest entry, and light management.
Treat drying as controlled moisture transfer with spatially variable temperature, RH, airflow, and load density.
Separate water activity from moisture content and preserve lot identity through storage.

exercises.title: Site and microclimate survey
exercises.task: Map sun exposure, drainage, wind, cold-air pooling, water access, neighboring light, wildlife, pest history, pollen sources, and smoke/dust exposure for one outdoor or protected site.
exercises.deliverable: A completed outdoor site survey with three priority risks and the evidence for each.

exercises.title: Drying-room process record
exercises.task: Track temperature, RH, airflow state, room zone, lot identity, product observations, and process adjustments through a drying interval.
exercises.deliverable: A drying-room log that connects each adjustment to a recorded observation.

capstone.title: Environment-to-storage process map
capstone.brief: Connect preharvest environment, harvest handling, drying, equilibration, packaging, and storage into one traceable process.
